vibe: Patch queues dominate: chained Zammad flaws and SharePoint ransomware need attention, while AI safety resignations and agent-era permission changes set the wider tone.

cyber.title: CISA flags chained Zammad RCE-to-root flaws as actively exploited
cyber.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-102489 and CVE-2026-102490 to KEV after active exploitation. The flaws can be chained from session fixation and remote code execution as the Zammad user to local root; operators should update and investigate exposed support systems now.

cyber.title: Warlock exploits SharePoint flaws to disable security tools and deploy ransomware
cyber.summary: Warlock ransomware crews are abusing SharePoint vulnerabilities, then disabling security tooling before encryption. The campaign overlaps yesterday's warnings and keeps SharePoint patching and compromise-hunting at the top of the queue.

cyber.title: Vercel bounty program confirms a KVM zero-day
cyber.summary: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch says the company's bounty program confirmed a KVM zero-day. Public detail is still thin, but operators running KVM-based infrastructure should watch vendor and distro advisories closely.

cyber.title: Apple tightens macOS Full Disk Access as AI agents raise the stakes
cyber.summary: Apple is narrowing how apps retain Full Disk Access because autonomous agents can turn broad local permissions into much larger data-exposure paths. It is a practical prompt to review desktop-agent privileges and consent flows.

cyber.title: Danish university breach exposes data of up to 200,000 people
cyber.summary: DTU says a breach may have exposed personal data belonging to as many as 200,000 people. The scale makes it notable, though the immediate technical lessons remain limited pending more detail.

ai.title: OpenAI safety employee resigns, saying the company's culture is broken
ai.summary: A departing OpenAI safety employee alleges that commercial and release pressure has overwhelmed internal safety culture. The Verge and Engadget independently covered the resignation, making this more than a single-source personnel story.

ai.title: Anthropic's Mythos bug-hunting model finds a vulnerability now under attack
ai.summary: Anthropic's specialist Mythos model reportedly helped uncover a mathematically subtle vulnerability that is now being exploited. It is a consequential proof point for AI-assisted vulnerability research—and for the shrinking time between discovery and attack.

ai.title: Meta open-sources code for building Muse AI gadgets
ai.summary: Meta released code intended to help developers build devices around Muse. The move broadens experimentation with ambient AI hardware beyond a single first-party product.

ai.title: Prime Intellect launches serverless and reserved inference for open models
ai.summary: Prime Inference offers serverless and reserved serving for frontier open models. It is worth tracking as another attempt to make open-model deployment feel like a mainstream managed cloud service.

ai.title: Open-source LEGO AI generator turns prompts into LDraw models
ai.summary: LDraw Nova is a playful but technically interesting open-source system for generating structured LEGO designs rather than flat images.

it.title: Cloudflare launches an Oblivious HTTP gateway
it.summary: Cloudflare's OHTTP gateway separates request origin from request content, giving developers a practical privacy layer for telemetry, AI and other sensitive API traffic. Strong Hacker News interest suggests useful real-world scrutiny.

it.title: FTL proposes a new operating system for clouds
it.summary: FTL is an ambitious attempt to treat distributed cloud resources as a coherent operating system. It is early, but relevant to cloud engineers interested in abstractions above today's VM, container and orchestration layers.

it.title: Cloudflare opens more formerly Enterprise-only features
it.summary: Cloudflare is moving additional capabilities down-market, potentially changing the build-versus-buy equation for smaller infrastructure teams.

videos.title: Your Cloud Security Is Missing Context
videos.verdict: SKIM — potentially useful cloud-security framing, but no transcript was available so confidence is limited.
videos.summary: The title points to the familiar gap between isolated security alerts and workload, identity and business context. Metadata only; no transcript was available for a full assessment.
